title: Quantization Profile Library: Validation & Quality Gates
author: Selene Huang
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the validation methodology and quality gates required to publish a **Redwood-issued Quantization Profile** into the Quantization Profile Library.

The goals of the gates are:
- Prevent **workload-specific quality regressions** (especially structured output / tool-calling).
- Ensure profiles are **safe to operate** (correct scoping, compatibility, fallback behavior) and **auditable**.
- Ensure profiles provide **meaningful unit-economics improvement** relative to baseline.

This is the authoritative checklist for Applied ML, Runtime, and SRE sign-off prior to publishing or promoting a profile.

## Definitions
- **Baseline**: the default (typically bf16/fp16) serving path for a given model version and serving runtime.
- **Quantized variant**: int8/int4 (or other) execution path defined by a quantization profile.
- **Profile**: a signed, versioned artifact in the model registry that includes quantization method, kernel constraints, hardware scope, calibration notes, and expected deltas.
- **Prompt set**: a curated dataset of prompts + expected evaluation method used by eval-harness.
- **Blocking metric**: a metric that, if failing threshold, prevents publish.
- **Non-blocking metric**: a metric tracked and reported; may be waived with an approved exception.

## Gate overview (what must pass to publish)
A profile may be published to the library only if it satisfies **all** of the following:
1) **Schema + integrity checks** (profile manifest valid; signing verified; required metadata present).
2) **Compatibility checks** (hardware/kernel constraints validated; runtime fallback path verified).
3) **Offline quality evaluation** (baseline vs quantized) across required prompt sets.
4) **Structured output / tool-calling robustness checks** (JSON validity, schema adherence).
5) **Safety checks** (policy compliance signals; toxicity/PII leakage indicators within thresholds).
6) **Performance & cost gates** (measured improvements meet minimum thresholds on supported GPU SKUs).
7) **Operational readiness** (telemetry tags present; rollback levers tested; canary plan documented).
8) **Approval workflow complete** (Required reviewers have explicitly approved; waivers documented if used).

## Required inputs for review
Each profile publish request (PR in model registry + associated change in inference config if needed) must include links/attachments to:
- Eval-harness run ID(s) for **quality comparison** (baseline vs quantized) covering the required prompt sets below.
- Perf suite report(s) for the **supported GPU matrix** (p50/p95 latency, throughput, tokens/sec, $/1M tokens estimate).
- A short **Profile Summary** (see template below).
- Any **known limitations** and recommended route-level policy defaults (e.g., “disable for JSON-mode routes”).

### Profile Summary template (required in PR description)
Include the following in the PR description:
- Model family + exact model version (registry ref)
- Profile ID + semantic version (e.g., qpl://llama-3.1-70b/int4-awq/v1.2.0)
- Quantization type (int8 / int4; method: AWQ/GPTQ/SmoothQuant/etc.)
- Supported GPU(s) and constraints (e.g., “H100 only; SM90; kernel=marlin-int4”) 
- Calibration notes (dataset, sample size, sequence length regime used for calibration)
- Expected deltas (cost, latency, throughput) and where they were measured
- Risk notes (known weak areas: long context, tool calling, code, etc.)
- Suggested initial rollout policy (recommended canary %, routes to exclude)

## Prompt sets: required coverage
We require coverage across multiple workload shapes. A profile must be evaluated on **at least the Minimum Set** for its target deployment tier.

### Minimum Set (required for all profiles)
1) **General Chat / Instruction Following**
- Purpose: detect general helpfulness regression.
- Example evals: pairwise judge win-rate; rubric scoring on helpfulness/groundedness.

2) **Summarization (short + long)**
- Purpose: common cost-optimization target; regression often subtle.
- Includes: factual consistency checks + compression ratio constraints.

3) **Structured Output (JSON mode)**
- Purpose: detect formatting failures which are high-severity in production.
- Includes: JSON parse validity + schema adherence.

4) **Tool Calling / Function Invocation**
- Purpose: detect tool argument formatting and selection drift.
- Includes: tool choice accuracy + argument validity.

5) **Long Context Stability**
- Purpose: quantization can degrade attention precision; long context is a frequent failure mode.
- Includes: at least one prompt set with context >= 16k tokens (or model max-context-1 bin if smaller).

### Additional required sets by profile type
- **int4 profiles**: Must additionally run **Code**, **Math/Reasoning**, and **Adversarial Robustness** prompt sets.
- **Profiles scoped to “assistant-critical” routes** (interactive chat): Must run **Safety/Refusal** and **Hallucination-sensitive QA** prompt sets.
- **Customer-specific enabled beta** (even if library is Redwood-issued): Add that customer’s agreed-upon prompt set pack if available.

### Prompt-set versioning and freshness
- Prompt sets are versioned (e.g., PS-JSON-2.1). The run must use prompt sets from the **current “recommended” channel** at the time of publish.
- Any prompt set older than **60 days** requires explicit confirmation from the Evals owner (Jonas Weber) that it is still representative.

## Evaluation methodology (offline)
All quality comparisons must be run through eval-harness using the “baseline vs quantized” runner.

### Required run configuration
- Run both baseline and quantized with:
  - Same model version
  - Same decoding parameters (temperature/top_p/max_tokens)
  - Same system prompt
  - Same tool schemas (if applicable)
- Use fixed seeds where supported and report variance.
- For streaming endpoints, evaluate on final assembled output.

### Reporting requirements
Eval reports must include:
- Aggregate deltas (overall and per prompt-set)
- Per-metric deltas
- Distribution summaries (mean/median) and confidence intervals where applicable
- Failure exemplars (top 20 largest regressions, with prompt IDs)
- “Structured output failures” list (prompt IDs where JSON invalid or schema violated)

### Statistical tests
- For win-rate style comparisons (e.g., judge preference): use a two-sided test with confidence level **95%** and report the CI.
- For rate-based metrics (JSON validity, refusal correctness): use Wilson interval reporting and enforce absolute thresholds.

## Quality gates (blocking)
Unless otherwise specified, thresholds apply:
- **Overall** across all required prompt sets
- **Per prompt set** (to avoid hiding a regression in a niche workload)

### A) General quality regression (blocking)
At publish time, the quantized variant must satisfy:
- **Overall preference win-rate vs baseline**: not worse than baseline by more than **1.0 percentage point** (pp).
- **Any individual prompt set**: not worse by more than **2.0 pp**.

Notes:
- If a model family lacks reliable judge evaluation, use the approved rubric metric for that family (tracked in eval-harness). This must be pre-approved by the Evals owner.

### B) Structured output correctness (blocking, stricter)
For prompt sets labeled structured-output/JSON-mode:
- **JSON parse validity rate**: must not drop by more than **0.2 pp** absolute.
- **Schema adherence rate** (if a schema is defined): must not drop by more than **0.5 pp** absolute.
- Any new failure mode producing “almost-JSON” (e.g., trailing commentary, markdown fences) at a rate > **0.1%** is blocking.

Rationale: JSON/tool failures are disproportionately harmful in production and are a primary reason quantization remains opt-in and route-scoped.

### C) Tool calling correctness (blocking)
For tool-calling prompt sets:
- **Correct tool selection rate**: must not drop by more than **0.5 pp** absolute.
- **Argument validity** (parseable + schema-valid): must not drop by more than **0.5 pp** absolute.

### D) Long-context degradation (blocking)
For long-context prompt sets (>=16k where applicable):
- **Any long-context set** must not regress more than **1.0 pp** on its primary metric.
- If the long-context set uses a composite score, any component designated “precision-critical” must not regress more than **0.5 pp**.

### E) Safety signals (blocking)
All safety checks must be within the envelope of baseline:
- **Policy compliance / refusal correctness**: must not regress more than **0.5 pp** on refusal-correctness sets.
- **Toxicity / hate / harassment flags**: no statistically significant increase; and absolute increase must be < **0.2 pp**.
- **PII leakage heuristic**: no statistically significant increase; any new “high confidence PII” exemplar is blocking until reviewed.

Notes:
- These are model- and prompt-set-dependent; the gating mechanism relies on our standardized classifiers + curated red-team prompt sets.

## Performance & cost gates (blocking)
A profile must demonstrate meaningful improvement on the GPU/hardware scope it claims.

### Required benchmarks
- Must run perf suite on all GPU SKUs listed in the profile’s supported matrix (or a documented subset for beta, explicitly marked).
- Must include at least three sequence length bins:
  - Short (e.g., 0–512 prompt tokens)
  - Medium (e.g., 512–4k)
  - Long (e.g., 4k–16k or max-context-1)
- Must include at least two load shapes:
  - Latency-sensitive (low concurrency)
  - Throughput-sensitive (high concurrency)

### Minimum improvements (blocking)
For the primary intended bin(s) listed in the profile summary:
- **Cost**: estimated $/1M output tokens must improve by **>= 15%** relative to baseline.
- AND one of:
  - **Throughput** (tokens/sec) improves by **>= 20%**, or
  - **p95 latency** improves by **>= 10%** under the latency-sensitive load shape.

Guardrail:
- No bin may regress p95 latency by more than **10%** unless explicitly marked as “unsupported” (and the profile is scoped to exclude it).

## Compatibility & correctness gates (blocking)
### Hardware scoping correctness
- The profile must explicitly define supported hardware constraints (e.g., SM versions, GPU models, driver/CUDA minimums where relevant).
- Runtime must log a “resolved profile” event with:
  - profile_id, profile_version
  - kernel path chosen
  - hardware class
  - compatibility decision (pass/fail) and reason code

### Fallback behavior
- When profile resolution fails (artifact missing, incompatibility, signature verify failure), the runtime must:
  - fall back to baseline
  - emit a structured metric/log with reason code
  - NOT increase 5xx rate due to profile issues

To validate:
- Include at least one negative test run in staging (or dedicated validation environment) that exercises an intentional incompatibility and confirms clean fallback.

### Artifact integrity (security requirement)
- Profile artifacts must be signed. Signature verification must be enabled in all environments where the profile is eligible.
- Any unsigned artifact or signature verification bypass is blocking for publish.

## Non-blocking checks (reported; may be waived)
The following are tracked and should be improved where possible, but are not always blocking:
- Minor style regressions (verbosity, tone) where product impact is low
- Small increases in “nonsense” or “repetition” classifiers when not tied to customer-visible failures
- Task-specific drops on low-priority prompt sets (explicitly labeled “informational”)

Any waiver must follow the exception process below.

## Exception / waiver process
We allow exceptions in limited cases to unblock targeted savings while keeping operational safety.

### When waivers are allowed
- Regression is confined to a clearly defined class of routes (e.g., JSON-mode) and the **recommended policy** disables those routes.
- Regression is small, well-characterized, and does not impact safety/structured output.
- Performance/cost benefit is high and the target customer/workload is compatible.

### Waiver requirements
A waiver must include:
- Metric(s) waived and observed delta(s)
- Impact analysis (which workloads/routes affected)
- Mitigation plan (route policy default, documentation note, monitoring alert)
- Expiration date (max 45 days) and follow-up ticket

Approvals required for waivers:
- Applied ML sponsor (Dr. Maya Srinivasan) OR delegate (Karthik Iyer)
- Evals/perf lead (Jonas Weber)
- Runtime lead (Mateo Alvarez) if compatibility or fallback behavior is implicated

## Approval workflow (publish + promote)
### Roles
- **Profile author**: Applied ML engineer responsible for calibration, evals, and PR.
- **Evals owner**: validates methodology and signs off on gating.
- **Runtime owner**: validates kernel constraints, compatibility, and fallback.
- **SRE reviewer**: validates monitoring and rollback readiness.

### Step-by-step
1) **Draft profile PR opened** (model registry)
   - Includes Profile Summary, artifacts, and initial scope.
2) **Automated checks**
   - Schema validation
   - Signature verification
   - Basic lint: required fields, semantic versioning rules
3) **Eval-harness quality run (required)**
   - Attach run IDs + report links to PR.
4) **Perf suite run (required)**
   - Attach perf reports for the supported GPU matrix.
5) **Human review + sign-off**
   - Applied ML: methodology + calibration notes
   - Evals/perf: metrics + thresholds
   - Runtime: compatibility + kernel selection
   - SRE: rollout/rollback plan readiness
6) **Publish** (library)
   - Profile becomes available for opt-in route-level enablement.
7) **Promote to “recommended” channel (optional, post-beta)**
   - Requires additional evidence from production canary metrics (see below).

## Canary validation (required for promotion; recommended for initial publish)
While initial library publish is offline-gated, promotion to broader availability requires production evidence.

### Minimum canary requirements
- Start at **1–5%** traffic on a non-critical route (or equivalent shadow traffic), then increase.
- Monitor for at least **24 hours** (or 1M requests, whichever is smaller) across at least two regions if applicable.

### Canary monitoring signals (blocking for promotion)
- 5xx rate: no increase > **0.05 pp** absolute
- JSON/tool failure rate (where applicable): no increase > **0.1 pp** absolute
- Latency p95: no regression > **5%** on the canaried route(s)
- Customer-reported incidents: none attributable to profile

If any of the above triggers, follow the rollback runbook and open an incident review if customer-impacting.

## What to do when a gate fails
1) Identify whether failure is:
   - Prompt-set specific (e.g., JSON-mode only)
   - Length-regime specific (e.g., long context)
   - Hardware specific (kernel mismatch)
2) Decide remediation:
   - Adjust quantization method/calibration
   - Narrow hardware scope
   - Narrow supported sequence-length regime
   - Recommend route exclusions
3) Re-run eval-harness + perf suite after changes.

## Ownership and ongoing maintenance
- Applied ML owns keeping profiles accurate and re-validating when:
  - Model version changes
  - Runtime/kernel changes materially affect execution
  - Hardware matrix expands
- Evals team owns prompt-set health and ensuring prompt sets remain representative.
- SRE owns the rollback runbook and alerting policy for quantization regressions.

### Scheduled re-validation
- Re-run quality + perf gates at least every **90 days** for profiles in the “recommended” channel.
- Re-run immediately for any major runtime release that changes kernel selection or batching behavior.

## Appendix: Severity guidance
- **Severity 0 (never waive)**: safety regressions, JSON/tool correctness regressions, signature/integrity failures, fallback failures.
- **Severity 1 (rarely waive)**: long-context regressions impacting supported bins, >10% p95 latency regression in supported bins.
- **Severity 2 (may waive)**: small general quality regressions with route scoping mitigations and strong cost wins.
